Your objective is to MAXIMIZE the reaction yield — the percentage of the limiting substrate converted to the desired coupled product.

You control the following parameters (each with its physical role and allowed range):

  - res_time — residence time (range [60, 600] s): how long reagents spend in the reactor — longer allows more conversion but also more catalyst decomposition and side-reactions
  - temperature — reactor temperature (range [30, 110] deg C): raises the reaction rate but can degrade the catalyst or promote side-pathways

turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**Ligand choice.** Ranking the best result per ligand at high temperature and high loading:
- **L3 → 98.7 %** (also 83.9, and 91.3/83.1 at low loading with long time) — clearly the top performer, and it is the only ligand that gives good yields across two different regimes (long time/low loading *and* short time/high loading).
- L6 → 85.4, L0 → 69.6, L2 → 62.8, L4 → 47.6, L1 → 41.9, L5 → 8.5. L5 is essentially dead.

**Temperature.** Every row at 30 °C gives the ~0.6 % baseline, and 65–69 °C only reaches 20–30 %. Yield rises monotonically to 110 °C for all ligands — the oxidative-addition/transmetalation barrier dominates, and no thermal-decomposition penalty is visible even at the top of the range. So push **T = 110 °C**.

**Catalyst loading.** At fixed L3/110 °C/600 s, ~1.1–1.27 mol% gives 72–91 %; at ~2.51 mol% with only ~190 s it gives 98.7 %. More Pd raises the turnover rate so the required residence time drops — and short contact time limits catalyst death and protodeboronation/homocoupling side-paths. Use loading near the **top of the range (~2.5 mol%)**.

**Residence time.** With L3 at 110 °C and 2.5 mol%, 190 s → 98.7 % while 200 s → 83.9 % (run-to-run scatter, but no gain from going longer), and 600 s at high loading was never needed. Long times at high T/high Pd promote Pd-black formation and product/boronic-acid degradation. The optimum sits in the **~180–220 s** window; I'll pick just around the best observed point, nudging slightly up to ensure full conversion without entering the decomposition-dominated long-time regime.

**Proposed optimum:** L3, ~195 s, 110 °C, maximum Pd loading — the same basin as the 98.7 % point with loading pushed marginally higher to buy back a little rate margin.

**Final: ligand=L3, res_time=195, temperature=110, catalyst_loading=2.515**
